data.name: Dharmakant
data.gender_notes: Dharmakant is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A name that signifies one who carries out his dharma or duty towards the society, his family, and the divine. It is a powerful name that is often found in Hindu mythology and scriptures. The name Dharmakant carries the meaning “Dharma (duty) Kant (carrier)” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dharmakant usually hope their child will grow to embody dharma (duty) kant (carrier) and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the pursuit of righteousness and duty towards oneself and others.
data.etymology: Dharmakant belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Dharma (duty) Kant (carrier).”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dharmakant total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

historical_references.reference: Dharmakant was the name of the famous Jain saint, Haribhadra Suri. He lived between 7th and 8th century CE and is considered as one of the greatest scholars of Jainism. He wrote several religious texts, including the 'Haribhadra-bindu-shastra'. This work is an important source of Jain logic and epistemology.

Dharmakanta was the name of a powerful king who ruled the Vatsa kingdom around 4th century BCE. He is mentioned in several Buddhist texts, particularly the 'Ashokavadana', where he is described as a great patron of Buddhism. He is said to have built several stupas and funded the construction of the Bodhi tree in Bodhgaya.
